quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 guidance: total revenue between $505 million and $545 million and EPS in the range of $0.18 to $0.34; 2026 tax rate expected in the low 20% range. Brian Harding (answering the margin questions for the company): Q1 gross margin roughly the same as Q4, maybe slightly up, then sequentially up through the year, with meaningful sequential margin expansion in Q2, Q3 and Q4 as volumes come in. CEO: utilization will be much higher by the end of 2026, and UCT will not grow OpEx and IDL as revenue grows.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenue between $505 million and $545 million; EPS $0.18 to $0.34

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity / ramp readiness (CEO and CFO): facility optimizations leave capacity in place to support approximately $3 billion in revenue today, with global utilization currently averaging 65%. About 50% of worldwide capacity is in Asia, with plans to increase to 60% to match key customers' global manufacturing footprint; the CEO expects the Asian factories to fill completely very soon. Only modest incremental clean room investment is required to support the long-term $4 billion annual run rate goal, and infrastructure capacity is not expected to be a limiting factor this cycle. Customers are encouraging UCT to position capacity ahead of the inflection, the largest customers are providing extended visibility, and UCT has identified and addressed product-specific supply chain and manufacturing constraints to be ready for a step function increase in orders. Ramp readiness is the top priority of the 'UCT 3.0' strategy, alongside an expanded MPX strategy (new product introduction, new product development, new product transition) to co-innovate earlier at leading-edge nodes.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $3 billion capacity; 65% utilization; approximately 50% of capacity in Asia, planned 60%; $4 billion annual run rate goal

quarterly_data.signal: WFE outlook (CEO): forecasts are increasing week by week, and UCT's overall WFE view is now 15% to 20% year-over-year growth, bigger than a month earlier. 2026 demand is second-half weighted and increases into 2027: growth already in Q2, then a step function increase in the second half of 2026 with a big bump from Q3 to Q4. The CEO is confident UCT revenue growth will be on par with WFE growth or even higher, capturing pull-in and drop-in opportunities with its extra capacity.

Technology drivers (CEO): industry projections suggest semiconductors could reach $1 trillion in annual revenue by 2027, possibly earlier. Leading-edge fabs are deploying new materials like molybdenum and new structures such as gate-all-around and high-bandwidth memory, raising deposition/etch capex intensity. UCT expects strength around etch and deposition, especially ALD and high-precision etch, to support gate-all-around and backside power distribution logic transitions as well as high-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging and greater than 300-layer NAND. A multiyear WFE upturn should follow once wafer fabs address their near-term clean room constraints.
quarterly_data.figure: semiconductor market $1 trillion in annual revenue by 2027 (industry projection); greater than 300-layer NAND

quarterly_data.signal: Memory cycle (CEO): some of UCT's customers' customers say the shortage will last until 2028; Micron, Samsung and SK are investing in greenfield fabs while converting existing fabs to address immediate demand, a multiyear upturn for memory. HBM will compromise the nameplate capacity in DRAM factories, so more WFE investment is needed to compensate while makers still address the unbalanced supply and demand in regular DRAM. NAND upgrades from 2xx to 3xx and 4xx layers continue; the CEO cited Lam's talk of $40 billion over multiple years of NAND upgrade investment, and said customers see a 22% CAGR for AI-specific memory (2 to 3x the regular memory market).
quarterly_data.figure: memory shortage until 2028 (per customers' customers); $40 billion multiyear NAND upgrade (Lam, as cited by the CEO); AI-specific memory 22% CAGR (per customers)

quarterly_data.signal: China (CEO): customers expect China WFE to be flattish in 2026, so China's share of worldwide WFE will fall as global WFE grows substantially; UCT's forecast for its China OEM business is also flattish for 2026, and China is less than 7% of UCT's overall revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: China less than 7% of overall revenue; China OEM business flattish in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Services (CEO): the Services business, driven by wafer starts, is expected to grow double digits in 2026, weighted to the second half as leading-edge foundry logic customers ramp their factories in the U.S.; UCT says it is well positioned for that U.S. foundry logic ramp in addition to the current U.S. customer it serves.
quarterly_data.figure: Services double-digit growth in 2026, second-half weighted
